solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Bosses to lead American fools (3,7)

blocks.note: to top the bill is to lead it
a banana is US slang for a silly person

annotation.surface: Someone complains that the people in charge are steering the country behind a pack of American idiots.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads "to lead" as bosses guiding fools; here it is the verb TOP, as in top the bill.
annotation.definitionFit: Top bananas are the most important people in an organisation, the bosses.

entries.clue: Walk far from streetcar with parking (5)

blocks.note: streetcar is the American word for a tram
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

annotation.surface: Someone decides to walk a long way rather than take the streetcar, parking included.
annotation.walkthrough: "Walk far from streetcar" reads as avoiding the tram; in fact the tram is inside the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk a long distance, usually heavily.

entries.clue: Stormy signs poor in forecast (9)

indicatorNotes.Stormy: a stormy mix is a turbulent one, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: the letters of SIGNS POOR rearranged

annotation.surface: A weather forecast shows bad omens of a coming storm.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stormy" looks like weather to match "forecast", but it only tells you to rearrange SIGNS POOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a forecast of how something, usually an illness, will turn out.

entries.clue: Park keeper losing head in fury (5)

indicatorNotes.losing head: the head of a word is its first letter, so it drops off

blocks.note: a park ranger looks after a park
RANGER without its first letter R

annotation.surface: A park keeper loses his temper.
annotation.walkthrough: "Losing head" sounds like losing one's temper, which suits fury; here it just removes the R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fury is anger at its most violent, which is what the surface's keeper is feeling.

entries.clue: Ottoman officer edges away from infidel (3)

indicatorNotes.edges away from: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, which go away

blocks.note: a pagan is an unbeliever
PAGAN without its outer letters P and N

annotation.surface: A Turkish officer backs cautiously away from an unbeliever.
annotation.walkthrough: "Edges away" reads as moving off slowly; it means removing the edge letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An aga was a military commander or official in the Ottoman Empire.

entries.clue: A person from eastern Europe protecting Saint Augustine? (7)

indicatorNotes.protecting: a guard protecting something stands all around it

blocks.note: taken as it stands
a Pole comes from Poland
ST is the usual abbreviation for saint

annotation.surface: A Polish bodyguard shields the saint named Augustine.
annotation.walkthrough: "Saint Augustine" reads as one name, but it splits: "Saint" is ST in the wordplay and "Augustine?" alone is the definition. The question mark marks him as one example of an apostle.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Augustine of Canterbury, who brought Christianity to England in 597, is called the Apostle of the English.

entries.clue: Footballer in red? (4-6)

blocks.note: a player on the left wing
a red is a socialist, someone on the political left

annotation.surface: A footballer playing in a red kit.
annotation.walkthrough: "In red" suggests a team's shirt colour; "red" is really a political socialist, and the question mark flags that it is only one kind of left-winger.
annotation.definitionFit: A left-winger is both a wide attacking footballer on the left and a person of left-wing politics.

entries.clue: Returned books are an inspiration (5)

indicatorNotes.Returned: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: Library books brought back are said to be inspiring.
annotation.walkthrough: "Returned books" reads as library books; "Returned" acts on OT and ARE together.
annotation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of love poetry, and a muse is a source of inspiration.

entries.clue: Alluring charm Olga ruined with rum (7)

indicatorNotes.ruined: ruined things are wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as it stands
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: Olga's allure is spoilt by too much rum.
annotation.walkthrough: "With rum" adds RUM to OLGA; both words are rearranged together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: glamour is the allure that makes a person or thing attractive, and it once meant a magic spell, a charm.

entries.clue: Corner at 90? (5,5)

blocks.note: the surface wants a street or football corner; the setter means where two lines meet
the 90 is degrees, not an age or a speed

annotation.walkthrough: "At 90" sounds like an age or a speed; it is 90 degrees, and a square corner is a right angle.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: two lines meeting squarely at 90 degrees form the geometric angle named here.

entries.clue: Pundit ran amok in cricket game (3-3-3)

indicatorNotes.amok: running amok is running wild, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: the letters of PUNDIT RAN rearranged

annotation.surface: A commentator goes wild during a cricket match.
annotation.walkthrough: Tip-and-run is an informal cricket game where the batter must run every time the bat touches the ball.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is one informal version of cricket, played on beaches and in back gardens.

entries.clue: Tent fire disturbed India’s ancient queen (9)

indicatorNotes.disturbed: disturbed things are moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as it stands
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A fire in a tent disturbs an ancient queen of India.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes her India's queen; "India's" just adds I, and the queen is Egyptian.
annotation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was an Egyptian queen of the 14th century BC, wife of Akhenaten.

entries.clue: Yank in powerful boat (3)

blocks.note: to yank is to pull hard
a small strong boat that tows larger ships into harbour

annotation.surface: An American aboard a powerful boat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Yank" looks like an American; it is the verb, a sharp pull.
annotation.definitionFit: A tug is both a hard pull and a powerful towing boat.

entries.clue: Mischievous Zulu band quiet (6)

blocks.note: an impi is a regiment of Zulu warriors
SH is the call for quiet

annotation.surface: A mischievous band of Zulu warriors keeps quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: An impi is a Zulu fighting unit, a word crossword setters use often.
annotation.definitionFit: Impish means mischievous, like an imp.

entries.clue: One Charlie blocking Iberian city entrance (7)

indicatorNotes.blocking: something blocking a passage sits inside it

blocks.note: Porto is a city in Portugal
the Roman numeral for one
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A man called Charlie stands blocking the way into a Spanish or Portuguese city.
annotation.walkthrough: I and C go together inside PORTO, between T and O.
annotation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch with columns at the entrance of a building.

entries.clue: Influence two females echo in performance (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the letters go in the other word

blocks.note: an act is a performance
F is the abbreviation for female, twice
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet, the word whose first letter it is

annotation.surface: Two women's echoing voices shape a stage performance.
annotation.walkthrough: FFE goes inside ACT, after the A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to have an effect on someone's views or actions is to influence them.

entries.clue: Swimmer in Ghasri periodically (3)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of GHASRI

annotation.surface: A swimmer turns up now and then in a place called Ghasri.
annotation.walkthrough: Ghasri is a village on Gozo in Malta, a fitting place for a swimmer.
annotation.definitionFit: A gar, or garfish, is a long-snouted fish, so a swimmer.

entries.clue: Devil about to damage one do-gooder (9)

indicatorNotes.about: to be about something is to be around it

blocks.note: Satan is the Devil
to mar is to damage
the Roman numeral for one

annotation.surface: The Devil is about to harm a do-gooder.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads "about to" as "going to"; the two words split, and "about" alone is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A Samaritan, after the Good Samaritan parable, is someone who helps others.

entries.clue: Brothel-keeper married first man (5)

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
Adam was the first man in Genesis

annotation.surface: The woman running a brothel married her first husband.
annotation.walkthrough: "First man" suggests a first husband; it is Adam of Genesis.
annotation.definitionFit: A madam is a woman who runs a brothel.

entries.clue: Idea from Met about to seize heroin and ecstasy (5)

indicatorNotes.about: to turn something about is to shuffle it, so MET is rearranged
indicatorNotes.to seize: what seizes something holds it inside

blocks.note: MET rearranged
H is slang for heroin
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

annotation.surface: The Metropolitan Police plan to seize a haul of heroin and ecstasy.
annotation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police, which suits a drugs bust; the word itself is rearranged to TME and takes HE after the T.
annotation.definitionFit: A theme is the main idea of a piece of work.

entries.clue: Was monarch pelted reportedly? (7)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, so the answer sounds like the word

blocks.note: it pelted down means it rained heavily

annotation.surface: A question whether the king was pelted with something.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pelted" suggests things thrown at the king; it is heavy rain.
annotation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as monarch, so reigned means was monarch.

entries.clue: Head in large cask turned up (3)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning up runs the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer

annotation.surface: A head appears in a big barrel that was upended.
annotation.walkthrough: A tun is an old word for a very large cask, common in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: the head is called this in slang, as in going off one's nut.

entries.clue: Current arrangement just right (5)

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a deal is an arrangement

annotation.surface: The present agreement is exactly right.
annotation.walkthrough: "Current" reads as "present"; here it is electric current, I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something perfect for its purpose is exactly right for it.

entries.clue: Basic reality in Milton to be changed (6,4)

indicatorNotes.changed: the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of MILTON TO BE rearranged

annotation.surface: A plea that the harsh truths in Milton's poetry should be altered.
annotation.walkthrough: "To be changed" reads as one phrase, but TO BE are letters to rearrange along with MILTON; only "changed" is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The bottom line is the fundamental truth or deciding factor.
